text:
Maya: Heads up — canary rollout of runtime v2.14 started ~10m ago, we’re seeing a sustained p99 spike (~20% up) and a few timeouts on long-context jobs. canary at 5% traffic.

Raul: ack. which hosts/variants? any obvious kernel change?

Maya: It looks correlated with the kernel-selector tweak from last merge (commit abc1234). Selector now prefers the new fused-attn kernel for small batches, but the canary trace shows a lot of KV cache misses leading to longer per-token kernels.

Sam: perf-bot attached flame graphs earlier — CPU hotspot moved into kv_cache::evict_path and also more memcpy in fused path.

perf-bot: [graph] https://perf.redwood/internal/graphs/1781234567 — metrics: p50/p95 stable, p99 +20%. kv_cache_miss_rate jumped 3x.

Jen: CI perf was green tho? any diffs between CI config and prod runtime?

Sam: CI runs smaller seqs and cached warm paths, so it missed this combination: medium seqs + sporadic cache churn under bursty request pattern.

Raul: can we bisect quickly to confirm abc1234 is the culprit? Sam, can you run git bisect + reproduce harness against the canary workload?

Sam: on it. Running bisect locally with the replay harness (script: ./tools/replay --trace canary-2026-03-18). If we get a repro, will isolate diff.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused automatically (policy: perf-degrade > 10% p99 for 5min).

Maya: good. we should prevent automatic promotion until we fix. Also need to check A/B gating: current gate checks error-rate only; we need p99 latency in the gate.

Sam: bisect found fail -> commit abc1234 (kernel selector heuristic) + small allocator change. Reapplied prior selector -> p99 returns to baseline in local replay.

Raul: propose two options: 1) revert abc1234 fully and resume rollout 2) patch selector to prefer kernel X only for seq < 256, and add a TTL bump to KV cache to avoid churn. Which is faster?

Jen: Ops notes: a revert will require a normal rollback PR + deploy, ~20min. Patch might be faster but riskier if incomplete.

Maya: we should prefer minimal blast radius. revert abc1234 to cut the perf regression, then we can ship a safer selector patch behind a feature flag and add more canary checks.

Raul: agree. also add an immediate mitigation: lower default batch size for canary nodes to reduce fused kernel entry and KV churn (config change; no code deploy).

Sam: opened revert PR #4523. Also created hotfix config change to set batch.max_tokens=1024 for canary pool.

perf-bot: CI benchmark run for revert PR shows p99 back to baseline, KV miss rate normalized. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/pr/4523

deploy-bot: Revert PR #4523 merged and staged. Canary traffic remains at 5% pending health checks; auto-pause cleared.

Maya: after merge, metrics look good on canary for last 10m. p99 within +/-3% of baseline. Resuming gradual rollout to 20% with 5min hold per step.

Raul: follow-ups: (a) add p99 latency gating to rollout controller (b) add kv_cache_miss_rate as a signal (c) expand CI perf harness to cover medium-seq cache-churn traces (d) improve selector unit tests to cover edge pattern.

Jen: I'll own (a) with infra. Sam -> own (c) and (d). Maya -> create a postmortem with timeline + mitigations.

Sam: noted. I'll also add an automated bisect job that runs when perf-degrade fires and posts the first suspect commit to thread.

Maya: thanks. one more: let's tweak auto-rollback threshold: current is >10% p99 for 5m. Recommend configurable threshold by route (some QoS-sensitive routes should be 5%/2m).

Raul: agree. add config for per-route SLO guardrails. Ops, confirm we can implement in rollout controller next week.

Jen: can do.

Maya: final: tag runtime release notes and flag the selector heuristic as experimental until we have the extra testing. :eyes:

Raul: +1 :thumbsup:

Sam: closing loop on the bisect + tests this afternoon.

Maya: thanks all.

deploy-bot: Note: automatic rollback logic will be updated after infra change; current canary continues as manual + gated.
